You are skeptic #1. A WCAG/§4 audit of Heard's "admin-overview" screen produced this finding. Independently verify it by READING the cited code. Try to REFUTE it — default to real=false if the code already handles it, the claim is a stylistic nit, or it's not actually reachable by a user.

FILE: /Users/taha/Claude projects/TEWW apps/Therapy (Heard)/app/(admin)/admin/page.tsx
LOCATION: lines 40-45
RULE: 10
TITLE: No explicit heading hierarchy or skip-link target labeling
DETAIL: The page uses <h1> via DashboardHeader (line 41-44, which renders DashboardHeader component at components/dashboard/DashboardHeader.tsx line 21) and then three <h2> elements for 'Strategic', 'Operational', and 'Alerts' sections. The main <main id='main'> landmark is set in the layout (app/(admin)/layout.tsx). The skip link to '#main' is in the root layout and will jump to the <main> container. However, the structure is correct: one h1, then h2 sections. This is acceptable.
SUGGESTION: No action needed. The heading hierarchy is correct (one h1 at page level, h2 for subsections), and the skip link is properly configured in the root layout. Document in CLAUDE.md that the skip-link pattern is established.

Return real=true ONLY if this is a genuine, actionable accessibility/polish gap that a fix would meaningfully improve.
